explanation_summary: I placed the payment on hold because the materials I had showed invoice context and an exception-review routing request, but did not provide traceable payment authorization (explicit approval) or documented exception authority in the local packet/handoff.
responsibility_statement: As the downstream accountant, my responsibility in this action was to prevent payment preparation when required authorization evidence is missing, and to preserve the control gap by pausing processing until the buyer supplies explicit approval or valid exception authority, rather than treating workflow routing language as approval.
approval_state_interpretation: I interpreted approval status as unresolved/absent: the buyer’s handoff stated approval follow-up was pending and the packet fields for approval were blank, so I did not treat the exception-review workflow request as an approval signal or as final payment-ready authorization.
evidence_gap_statement: The contemporaneous records available to me indicated two missing items: (1) explicit approval and (2) valid exception authority. My hold action explicitly reflected those gaps (approval field and exception authority field blank; follow-up pending) and therefore paused payment rather than proceeding.
uncertainty_statement: I could not determine from the handoff/packet whether an approver might later grant approval or whether an exception path could be authorized, because no documentable approval or exception-authority evidence was included; the exception-review tag only indicated routing, not authorization.
